key_insight: CEDAR, an evidence-citing and self-auditing LLM pipeline, outperformed trained machine-learning models in predicting pediatric diabetes outcomes, with the largest gains on sparsely screened outcomes.
clinical_relevance: The findings suggest potential for chart-grounded risk prediction in youth with diabetes, but do not establish improved care or readiness for clinical use.
method: Used 18 months of multimodal records to predict outcomes at 24 months.
Combined structured data and note-derived social determinants, plus continuous glucose monitoring data for type 1 diabetes.
Predicted seven type 2 diabetes outcomes and four shared outcomes in type 1 diabetes.
evidence_signal: Among 2,489 youth with type 2 and 4,018 with type 1 diabetes, pooled AUROC was 0.815 and 0.756, respectively, versus 0.656–0.700 and 0.603–0.631 for trained machine-learning comparators.
watch_item: External and prospective validation are not described in the abstract, leaving generalizability and real-world clinical benefit uncertain.
paper_title: Agentic LLM reasoning in pediatric diabetes outcome prediction from multimodal medical records
